verdict_reason: Linear CKA reproduces the closed form ||Y^T X||_F^2 / (||X^T X||_F ||Y^T Y||_F) on column-centred inputs, reimplemented independently from the paper, over 20 random (n, d1, d2) shapes. Agreement is to ~7e-8 relative, which is float32 precision and is BY DESIGN: cka.py:23 narrows with M = M.float(), and float32 and float64 INPUTS return the identical value (0.13436627311433538 for both, against the exact float64 closed form's 0.13436626362814083). Promoting that arithmetic would be a regression against a bit-pinned reference under this repo's own gating rule, so it is recorded as a precision property rather than repaired. Structural invariants hold: CKA(X,X) = 1 to 1e-9, orthogonal invariance CKA(X, XQ) = 1 to 1e-6 for a random orthogonal Q, and scale invariance to 1e-6 at 1e-6, 1e3, 1e6. This verdict rests on an INDEPENDENT REIMPLEMENTATION of the reference, not only on executed parity.
